title: TokenDocument
description: A semantic, platform-neutral description of a Figma file's design-token variables, produced by the Figma plugin (which can resolve alias chains, real mode names, and imported library variables that a raw REST/plugin variables dump cannot). Companion to ir/v1/schema.json: that schema describes a *selection* of the scene graph and changes constantly; this one describes the *file's* tokens and changes rarely. Kotlin/codegen concerns (package names, class shapes, factory functions, build order) are deliberately NOT modelled here - this document carries Figma-side facts only.

collections.description: Every collection that survived the policy filter, in Figma's own declared order. A collection with zero variables is emitted as an empty `tokens` array rather than omitted, so 'this collection is empty' stays distinguishable from 'this collection disappeared'.

unresolved.description: Every variable that could not be fully represented, with a machine-readable reason. Producers MUST emit an entry here for any input variable not present in `collections` - a variable must never be silently dropped.

envelope.title: TokenDocumentEnvelope
envelope.description: Document-level provenance. Deliberately carries no timestamp: an export of unchanged content must be byte-identical to the previous one, which a wall-clock field would break.

schemaVersion.description: The token schema major version this document conforms to (currently 1).

kind.description: Discriminates this document from the node IR when both are handled by one consumer.

fileKey.description: The Figma file key these tokens came from.

version.description: A deterministic content hash of this document's own payload (see the plugin's versioning.ts). Opaque and comparable for equality only - not parseable or ordered. Equal versions mean identical content; a changed version means something a consumer can see actually changed.

policyReport.title: PolicyReport
policyReport.description: The exclusion policy that was actually applied, echoed into the document so an export is self-describing and a stale or mistyped pattern is visible in the artifact itself rather than only in the build log.

excludedCollections.description: Collection name patterns that were excluded (shell-style globs, matched case-insensitively).

excludedBranches.description: Branch patterns that were excluded. A pattern containing `/` matches `<collection>/<branch>`; a bare pattern matches that branch in every collection.

excludeRemoteCollections.description: Whether collections imported from other Figma libraries were excluded. Defaults to true: a real file's remote collections are overwhelmingly unrelated library noise, and their names collide with each other and with local collections.

unmatchedPatterns.description: Patterns that matched nothing. Reported rather than silently ignored, so a typo never turns into a silent no-op.

id.description: The Figma variable collection id. Carried once per collection rather than repeated on every token, and needed because collection *names* are not unique across imported libraries.

remote.description: True when this collection is imported from another Figma library rather than defined locally.

defaultMode.description: The name of the collection's default mode. Preserved because it encodes designer intent (which mode a single-value consumer should read) and is not recoverable from an alphabetically sorted mode list.

modes.description: Mode names in Figma's own declared order - NOT sorted. Order is meaningful content here, and sorting it destroys the default/primary-mode signal.

branches.description: The distinct first path segments present in this collection's tokens (e.g. ["color", "radius", "scale"]), in first-seen order. Observed structure, not a codegen decision - a generator may use it to shape classes, or ignore it.

dependsOn.description: Names of other collections this collection's tokens alias into, sorted for determinism. The observed alias-edge summary a build-order/graph step can be derived from, without this document itself modelling build order.

path.description: The raw Figma variable name, slash-separated, verbatim and unsanitized (e.g. "color/surface/action/primary/default"). Identical to the node IR's `TokenValue.token` for the same variable. NOT unique on its own - see the owning collection.

value.description: The resolved literal for the collection's DEFAULT mode. Colors are `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA` hex - the same representation the node IR uses, so the two documents' values for one variable are the same string. `null` means unresolvable in the default mode; the token then also appears in `unresolved`.

modes.description: Resolved literal per mode name, for every mode the owning collection declares. Always present (even for a single-mode collection) so consumers never have to special-case it.

scopes.description: Figma's variable scopes (e.g. ["CORNER_RADIUS"], ["GAP"], ["TEXT_FILL"]). This is how a consumer knows a FLOAT is a radius and not a gap - the intent signal that a bare number loses.

deleted.description: Figma's `deletedButReferenced`: the variable is deleted but something still points at it. Emitted (flagged) rather than dropped, so a consumer can decide.

symbol.description: The Kotlin design-system symbol, derived by evaluating mappings/wiring-rules/wiring-rules.yaml against (collection, path). Omitted when no rule confidently derives one - the normal case, and not an error.

symbolFrom.description: The id of the wiring rule that produced `symbol`, so any emitted symbol can be traced to the rule and evidence behind it.

aliasEdges.title: AliasEdges
aliasEdges.description: Where this token's value comes from, when it aliases another variable. The alias EDGE is the fact; a resolved literal is only a view of it. Leaf collections routinely have a single mode while aliasing into a multi-mode collection, so a flattened value silently collapses light/dark - preserving the edge is what lets a consumer expand modes correctly instead of reconstructing the graph from values.

byMode.description: Mode name -> the variable this token aliases in that mode. A mode with a literal (non-alias) value is absent.

collection.description: Name of the collection the aliased variable belongs to, or null when it could not be read.

path.description: The aliased variable's raw Figma name, or null when the target could not be resolved.

excluded.description: True when the alias points into a collection the policy excluded. The value then falls back to the resolved literal so generated code never references something that was not emitted - the documented behaviour this mirrors from the platform's collections.toml.

opacity.description: Set when this alias is a Figma "composed color" (a color variable with an opacity variable applied on top, e.g. "palette/slate/300 at 40%") AND the opacity itself is a named variable, not a bare literal - i.e. there is a second, real alias edge worth preserving, not just a number to bake into the resolved literal. Never itself carries a nested `opacity` (Figma does not support composing a composed color).

tokenHints.title: TokenHints
tokenHints.description: Non-authoritative signals carried for humans and coding agents. Nothing in the pipeline may RESOLVE against these - they are labelled as hints precisely so that a consumer cannot mistake them for a contract.

codeSyntax.description: Figma's per-platform `codeSyntax` for this variable (WEB/ANDROID/iOS). Useful as a naming hint when generating code, but deliberately NOT used to derive `symbol`: the platform is moving to a Styles API that will supply the real symbols, at which point these names could diverge.

unresolvedToken.title: UnresolvedToken
unresolvedToken.description: Records a variable that could not be fully represented. Mirrors the node IR's UnresolvedEntry convention: every unresolvable value MUST produce one of these rather than a silent substitution or omission.

reason.description: Stable machine-readable reason code. `missing-alias-target`: the aliased variable could not be read at all. `unresolvable-alias-chain`: circular or deeper than the hop limit. `excluded-collection-alias`: resolved, but through a collection the policy excluded (value falls back to the literal). `excluded-by-policy`: the variable itself was excluded. `unsupported-value`: a value shape this schema cannot represent.
